title: Explainable machine learning screens for carotid atherosclerosis from check-up data
summary: From 69,601 health check-up records at one hospital in Shenyang, ten machine learning algorithms were compared to screen for carotid atherosclerosis (6315 records had carotid ultrasonography). The gradient boosting decision tree model was best, with an auROC of 0.860 (95% CI 0.839 to 0.880) in the internal test set and 0.851 (0.837 to 0.863) in a temporally separate 2018 external set. Negative predictive value was low in people with diabetes or over 65, and SHAP ranked age, sex and non-HDL cholesterol highest.
ai_technology: Gradient boosting decision tree (best of ten ML algorithms) with SHAP on routine check-up indicators
